climate_hazard: Infectious disease: The Pest and Disease threat is considered to include outbreaks of diseases transmitted 1) directly from humans to humans (e.g., influenza, tuberculosis, COVID-19), 2) indirectly through vectors like mosquitoes and ticks, and 3) indirectly through food (e.g., shellfish) and water. This threat also includes pests such as rodents and invasive species like iguanas and Burmese pythons. Climate influences infectious disease transmission directly by affecting the biological processes of pathogens and vectors as well as indirectly by affecting their habitats. Warmer temperatures and more humid conditions are likely to provide more favorable conditions for vectors that are already present in a place. In addition, warmer temperatures are expected to result in northward expansion of the geographic range of many vectors. According to the ArboNET database maintained by the CDC, between 2015-2019, 114 cases of vector-borne diseases such as dengue, Zika and chikungunya were reported in Palm Beach County. The incidences vary significantly from year to year. Note that the CDC expects these numbers to be underestimated since the data is collected passively i.e., a case is registered in the database only when a clinician reports a confirmed diagnosis to the state public health officials. Based on the US Census Community Resilience Estimates, In Palm Beach County around 38% of residents have three or more risk factors and around 48% have one to two risk factors for infectious disease outbreaks. The City of Boynton Beach has several Census tracts with >50% of residents at risk. | Urban flooding: As climate change occurs, hydrologic shifts are likely causing increases to both the frequency and intensity of rainfall-induced flooding throughout South Florida. This threat is closely linked to and may exacerbate other climate threats that involve flooding. Rainfall-induced flooding is also exacerbated by several significant non-climate stressors such as changes to historical hydrology via land-use alteration, aging infrastructure, and the many challenges related to maintenance of stormwater infrastructure. Sea level rise is worsening rainfall-induced flooding in parts of Southeastern Palm Beach County where coastal stormwater sewer networks cannot discharge as designed. The threat of rainfall-induced flooding presents the greatest exposure and highest levels of vulnerability and risk of all flooding threats assessed in this study. Energy & Communications and Health & Medical assets have the highest percentage of highly vulnerable and at-risk properties (34% and 39% respectively). More than a third of all grocery stores, food SNAP retailers, and food pantries are vulnerable across the region. Public safety and government-owned assets are vulnerable. About 31% of all commercial and industrial properties being highly vulnerable and at risk. Residential property has the highest level of vulnerability and risk of all property types with 43% of all residential properties in the study area having medium-high combined vulnerability and risk associated with a 500-year storm event. About 44% of the residential properties exposed to rainfall-induced flooding have low adaptive capacity. Areas with high levels of residential physical vulnerability also co-occur with many of the most socially vulnerable areas of the region, based on the CDC's Social Vulnerability Index. About 50% of roads (both major and minor) and properties in the study area have the potential for inaccessibility in the 100-year rainfall-induced flooding scenario. The greatest increases in vulnerability to rainfall-induced flooding, as a result of future sea level rise, are to certain critical facilities (energy & communications, health & medical, and food infrastructure), residential, and commercial property, each with more than 10% potential increase in vulnerability from 2020 to 2070. | Other: Water-borne disease: Incidents of waterborne diseases are known to be associated with heavy precipitation events. For example, a study estimated that 68% of waterborne outbreaks in the U.S. over a period of 50 years were preceded by extreme precipitation events. More intense precipitation in a warming world has the potential to exacerbate the threat from waterborne diseases. According to Florida Department of Health, between 1997 to 2020, there were 2,610 cases and 264 incidents of food and waterborne diseases in Palm Beach County. Harmful Algal Blooms (HABs) occur when particular species of algae grow out of control, negatively impacting humans, fish, shellfish, marine mammals, and birds. HABs have occurred in recent years and have not only affected these natural systems, but they also have significant impacts on local economies. HABs are expected to start increasing in frequency and intensity. These increased blooms are related to increases in oceanic temperatures and changes to historical hydrologic patterns (e.g., changes in rainfall patterns). Non-climate stressors are also a significant factor in the production of HABs because they are linked to increased loads of nutrients entering waterways via stormwater runoff through both point source and non-point sources. Furthermore, as septic systems age and/or as groundwater inundation occurs, increased nutrient loads may originate from these septic systems. The assessment indicated that impairments and HABs are occurring in the study area and that these issues spatially interact. As more development occurs, increasing nutrient loads are also likely unless more strategic and scientific action is taken to address water quality in Boynton Beach and Palm Beach County. Addressing HABs will require a regional watershed approach, which is particularly challenging in Palm Beach County due to the relatively large number of jurisdictions that would need to participate. Palm Beach County is also just beginning to experience the regulatory activity involved in Total Maximum Daily Load (TMDL) development when compared to other regions throughout Florida. TMDLs have energized other local governments in Florida to develop cooperative and scientific watershed approaches because of the economy of scale that can be achieved and perhaps most importantly - because TMDLs can be very expensive for local governments to address. | Coastal flooding (incl. sea level rise): Tidal flooding, also referred to as “king tide,” “nuisance flooding” or “sunny day” flooding, occurs during non-storm periods and is due to high astronomical tides that occur periodically throughout the year. King tides generally refer to the highest tidal flooding events of the year and is a colloquial term. Tidal flooding can occur due to direct inundation of upland areas as well as through storm drain systems that cannot outfall (due to higher tidal elevations) and overflow into interior low-lying areas. This type of flooding can cause temporary interruptions in day-to-day activities through flooding of streets with saltwater and backing up of storm sewer systems that prevents drainage during even small rainfall events. When these high-tide events coincide with even small coastal storms or wind events, the flooding levels can be further exacerbated. As sea levels rise, the time periods when tidal flooding occurs will increase in frequency and duration. This will also be exacerbated by land subsidence and losses of natural barriers. Data has shown that tidal flooding has risen over the past few decades. Extents of water level increases under various sea level rise scenarios were assessed for the project area. While the overall levels of vulnerability and risk are not as high for tidal flooding compared to the other flood threats, it is important to keep in mind the impact from the frequency of tidal flooding, especially with future change, and the thresholds that will lead to more persistent flooding over time. It is also important to point out that if rain-induced or storm surge events were to take place during a King Tide event in a SLR scenario then the effects of flooding would be significantly exacerbated. Vulnerability is expected to increase over time for nearly every asset type in the study area. Vulnerability and risk to residential properties increases more than ten times between 2020 and 2070. Road connectivity related vulnerabilities (for both major and minor roads) have the greatest potential increase with future change and tidal flooding. In Boynton Beach, about $609 million in assessed property value is projected to be at risk by 2070. | Drought: Drought is prolonged dry period that can impact availability of water supply, agriculture, and other aspects of life. It is a significant threat since it relates to the basic human requirement for safe and adequate drinking water. Drought also creates significant impacts on natural systems, socioeconomics, and agriculture. This is a complex threat as it relates to several climate stressors and other threats (groundwater inundation, saltwater intrusion, and wildfires). Climate stressors that exacerbate drought primarily include increases in spatial and temporal variability in rainfall, increased global temperatures, and increased evapotranspiration. Changes in human populations - such as increased consumption of freshwater and human migration - also affect drought. The most recent prolonged droughts in Florida occurred between 2006 and 2008 and 1998 through 2002. During these periods of drought, rainfall was well below normal levels throughout the state, causing low streamflow and low groundwater levels. Water use varies throughout the year based on irrigation and population need, and when drier conditions occur, the demand for freshwater increases, putting stress on the groundwater aquifer system. In addition to water supply being at risk during periods of drought, the area becomes more susceptible to sink holes, wildfires, and saltwater intrusion. | Storm: Storm surge is the abnormal rise in sea level during a storm, measured as the height of the water above the normal predicted astronomical tide. The amplitude of the storm surge at any given location depends on the orientation of the coastline with the storm track; the intensity, size, and speed of the storm; and the local bathymetry. The risk under a storm surge event is exacerbated by local wave conditions, which can amplify the overall risk levels. Sea level rise can have the effect of increasing each of the different components beyond just the long-term sea level rise - e.g., waves are bigger in deeper water, storm surge can propagate in farther and higher when water levels are deeper. An assessment of storm surge ties with other identified threats in that storm surge is directly tied to rainfall-induced flooding through potential backflow during storm conditions. It is also directly tied to shoreline recession as higher storm surge, and the associated waves, are some of the key driving mechanisms. At current 2020 (100-year) storm surge inundation levels, percentages of vulnerability and risk are relatively low for the study area compared to rainfall-induced flooding. However, part of this is due to storm surge risk being concentrated along the coastal and intracoastal areas of the study area. Assets with the highest levels of vulnerability and risk to storm surge include parks and cultural, residential, and roads and mobility (including potentially inaccessible major roads, minor roads, and property). With future sea level rise, the assessment highlights that the percent of assets highly vulnerable and at risk to storm surge is likely to increase. The number of commercial and industrial properties with medium to high vulnerability and risk to storm surge more than double over the next 50 years from a total of 176 (5%) properties to 373 (10%) properties. Vulnerability and risk to critical facilities also increases steadily over time, especially for health & medical, energy & communications, and food infrastructure. Vulnerability related to road inaccessibility increases steadily starting from 8% for major roads and 9% for minor roads in 2020 and increasing over the next 50 years to 15% and 12% respectively. Residential property vulnerability and risk increases from about 7% in 2020 to 11% by 2070 (2020 baseline + 33” SLR). | Extreme wind: Sustained high winds are typically associated with tropical systems in Southeast Florida, and thus most common during hurricane season (June 1 through November 30). Sustained high winds can destroy infrastructure and other physical assets. As the climate warms, it is anticipated that the most intense hurricanes (Categories 3-5) will become more frequent, even though the overall frequency of hurricanes may not change. This means that the likelihood of a strong hurricane with high sustained winds hitting South Florida will increase. For this study, a screening-level assessment was developed for all properties in the study area to estimate vulnerability to high winds. This assessment shows properties that may be more vulnerable to high winds based on use type and relevant wind-related building design regulations at the time the primary structure on a property was built. Health & Medical and Parks & Cultural properties have the highest percentages of vulnerability to high winds (61% and 99%, respectively). Energy & Communication and Food Infrastructure also have high levels of vulnerability to high winds with more than a third (37% and 36%, respectively). About 11% of the residential properties in the region have medium or high vulnerability to high winds. Residential property vulnerability also has a high co-occurrence with socially vulnerable populations. For example, 18 of the 22 residential census tracts most vulnerable to high winds are also among the most socially vulnerable. | Extreme heat: Extreme heat events are periods of excessively hot and/or humid weather that can last multiple days. Extreme heat is a pressing public health risk, particularly for low-income and elderly communities living in developed areas with limited options for relief from heat. It also disproportionately impacts low-income households who may live in substandard housing and may not be able to afford air conditioning. According to Union of Concerned Scientists, Palm Beach County historically had four days per year with a heat index above 105 degrees F. On the current emissions pathway, this is projected to increase to 72 days by midcentury and 126 days by late century. A screening-level extreme heat vulnerability assessment was performed by examining land cover, sensitive populations, tree canopy cover, and socioeconomic stress. All of the CCVA study area was considered as being exposed to the potential for extreme heat. A ruleset-based approach was then developed for considering aspects of potential impact (focused on sensitive populations and developed land cover) and adaptive capacity which considers tree canopy coverage and socioeconomic vulnerability (based on the CDC's socioeconomic status theme, one component of their overall social vulnerability index). The most vulnerable census tracts were identified as 1) highly developed areas with higher percentages of sensitive residents (older than 65 or under 18), 2) those with relatively low tree canopy coverage and high socioeconomic stress. The City of Boynton Beach includes 10 census tracts with high vulnerability to extreme heat. | Other: Subsidence: Coastal erosion, which results in shoreline recession, is the process by which wave action, wind, sea level rise, and other factors wear down and transport soil and/or sand away from or along the coast. This is compounded in the study area by the disruption of sediment transport by coastal development, jetties, inlets, and hardened shorelines. In addition to longer term erosion processes, beaches in the region are prone to storm events that can worsen erosion impacts and lead to more serious shoreline recession. Sea level rise and climate threats are anticipated to exacerbate erosion in the future, especially as storms increase in intensity and frequency. Beaches in the study area are regularly maintained to mitigate the impacts of erosion and provide a level of storm protection for adjacent coastal areas. However, a changing climate will make these mitigation measures less effective over time if the maintenance procedures remain the same. The assessment found that under 2020 baseline conditions, the healthiest shorelines are found in areas having benefitted from long-term beach management programs that include beach nourishment and, where appropriate, inlet management. Shoreline recession associated with sea level rise further reduces the level of protection provided along the coast. The City of Boynton Beach is minimally impacted by this climate threat because there is no shoreline within the city limits. The City just manages its Oceanfront Park beach which is within the Town of Ocean Ridge. The shoreline is rated as poor to fair in this area, suggesting that further protective measures are needed to safeguard coastal assets. | Other: Saltwater intrusion: Saltwater intrusion and groundwater inundation are primarily connected to climate change through sea level rise. The freshwater aquifer in South Florida floats atop the saltwater below as a lens. The porous limestone allows the water to oscillate with sea levels. This will allow groundwater to breach the surface in low-lying areas, permanently inundating land. This is in addition to tidal flooding concerns. Most of the population in South Florida obtains their drinking water through the surficial aquifer systems, increasing vulnerability with sea level rise and a warming climate. While heavy rainfall can temporarily enhance groundwater levels, the sustained groundwater rise expected as part of sea level rise is a greater long-term threat. The combined threat of groundwater inundation and heavy rainfall-induced flooding will likely be the greatest concern for large-scale sustained flooding for the region. A primary concern associated with rising groundwater is decreased stormwater infiltration and therefore partial or complete failure of various stormwater systems. As rising sea levels cause groundwater levels to rise, the soils closer to the surface will be saturated and will have reduced storage capacity. This means that our methods of managing stormwater will need to be rethought and modified. Many of our stormwater systems were designed based on historical groundwater conditions and assumptions. This also means that designs for green infrastructure must take future conditions into account as the hydrology of our natural systems may also shift. Rising groundwater levels may also impact erosion rates, especially in low-lying coastal areas. Furthermore, coastal drinking water wells may become brackish due to saltwater intrusion. The City of Boynton Beach has pro-actively moved wells to the western part of the city to prevent saltwater intrusion. As sea level rises, septic tanks will fail. This is a significant issue across South Florida and can impact water quality and lead to harmful algal blooms. | Fire weather (risk of wildfires): This assessment examined the threat of wildfire in the Wildland Urban Interface (WUI), areas where homes and assets are within or adjacent to vegetation and fuels for wildfire. The risk of wildfire is greatest in years of drought. The peak wildfire season in Florida is typically January through mid-June, burning over 100,000 acres of land annually. Within Palm Beach County over the past 20 years there have been 10 wildfires over 10,000 acres in size. Lightning is one of the main causes of large wildfires on managed lands. The direct wildfire risk to people and assets in the CCVA study area is relatively low due to limited WUI areas, however the smoke generated from wildfires can impact air quality, which in turn impacts human health. Wildfire response capacity is also something that seems to be adequate throughout the study area, with all of the study area being within a 5-min drive time from the nearest fire station.
project_info: Nature-Based Solutions - Living Shoreline Project: Installation of living shorelines along water bodies prone to flooding. These bodies include the intracoastal waterway, lakes, and canals. The aim is to not only improve shoreline resilience during flooding, but reduce the impacts of sea level rise and improve water quality and habitat in these areas.

Power and water utilities face peak demand for cooling and supply, stressing electricity and water systems and reducing labour productivity across transport and education services. | Drought: Rainfall deficits reduce soil moisture and surface/groundwater availability, harming smallholder farmers, rural communities, low-income households and outdoor workers. Water utilities must pump/treat more with intermittent supply, increasing costs and service interruptions; knock-on effects appear in wastewater operations, power for pumping/cooling, health services and hospitality. | Fire weather (risk of wildfires): Hot, dry and windy conditions raise ignition and spread, threatening rural communities, outdoor workers, low-income and elderly groups with evacuation, smoke exposure and asset loss. project_info: Buildings - Marine Litter Dodge and Management / MALIDOMA: It is characterized by a complex system of coastal and marine ecosystems that are essential for the livelihood and well-being of millions of people. The region supports various economic sectors, including tourism, fisheries and maritime transport. However, increasing anthropogenic pressures, such as marine litter pollution, threaten the environmental integrity and economic sustainability of the region. Within the scope of the project, various activities will be carried out to develop innovative tools and methods for early detection, prevention and management of marine litter, to facilitate policy learning and dialogue on the prevention and management of marine litter at local, regional and national levels, and to create a solid network of stakeholders to solve the problem of marine pollution in Europe.\n

project_info: Transport - PUBLIC TRANSPORT ON THE ROAD TO ZERO CARBON: Antalya is one of the cities with the highest population growth in our country. Considering the number of registered vehicles, there is one vehicle for every two people. For this reason, according to the calculations made within the framework of the Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan (SECAP) implemented by our municipality, transport ranks second with a rate of 30.2% after building-related emissions. Considering the growth potential of Antalya, it is important to reduce carbon emissions within the scope of combating climate change, especially in this area, thanks to the support to be provided. The most important among the projects to be developed regarding transport is the development of Antalya's environmentally friendly public transport system. Making public transport more widespread and accessible can reduce the use of individual vehicles, reduce carbon emissions and alleviate traffic problems. There are already two electric buses in Antalya, purchased through the MatchUP project. The introduction of vehicles running on hydrogen fuel & biofuels (bioethanol, biomethane, biodiesel) or electric vehicles will help the city to increase the demand for public transport and reduce greenhouse gas emissions from transport. Vehicle to be purchased: 12 Meter hydrogen fuel & biofuels or electric bus. Qty: 20.

project_info: Water management - RENEWABLE ENERGY SOURCES IN WATER MANAGEMENT: 98% of Antalya's water supply is provided from groundwater sources and fossil fuelled electrical energy is used for this supply. Energy costs are increasing day by day in processes such as providing, transporting and treating these supplies. While 15.6% of ASAT Water and Wastewater Administration's expenses in 2018 were electricity expenses, this rate was 54% in 2022. This situation also increases carbon emissions. These challenges can be solved with renewable energy resources projects in water management to be realised with the support to be given in water management and water supply. These include:1. Utilization of renewable energy systems and development of the necessary infrastructure (roof type or storage solar energy systems, hydraulic pressure breaker energy systems), Places to build: Kumluca (4), Alanya (2), Termessos (1) Potential Budget: € 10 million 2. Supporting renewable energy and water resource creation technologies (treatment of seawater with solar energy and obtaining drinking water-desalination systems, water collection systems from atmospheric moisture, etc.) necessary for the commissioning of alternative water resources in a way to create infrastructures can provide improvements in water management. Places to be built: Korkuteli (1), Antalya centre (1) Potential Budget: € 3 million Euros

project_info: Waste management (including waste recycling) - ENVIRONMENTALLY FRIENDLY VEHICLES IN WASTE MANAGEMENT: The density of population and tourism activities in Antalya increases the amount of waste. The city is struggling with a demand for services beyond its capacity due to both tourism and increased migration. Added to this is the volume of waste generated by hotels, restaurants and other tourism facilities during the tourism season. Despite all this, Antalya Metropolitan Municipality provides transfer to waste collection facilities with approximately 45 trucks with a capacity of 30 tonnes. These trucks consume 1 litre of fuel oil per 2 km. And this process continues continuously. The development of environmentally friendly vehicles (hydrogen fuelled or electric trucks) in waste management with the support to be given is of great importance in terms of both reducing carbon emissions and reducing our costs. In addition, the fact that urban cleaning brooms, of which there are currently 6, are hybrid or electric instead of fossil fuel can also be evaluated within the scope of this project. Number of hydrogen fuelled or electric trucks to be purchased: 20 Potential Budget: € 10 million Number of hybrid or electric urban cleaning vacuum cleaners to be purchased: 24 Potential Budget: € 100 thousand

project_info: Health systems and services - Strategies for Mitigating the Urban Heat Island (UHI) Effect in Antalya (MUHIR): MUHIR is Antalya's flagship climate adaptation project under the Horizon Europe CLIMAAX program. It addresses the increasing risks of urban heat islands (UHIs) and heatwaves by: Developing a methodological framework to map and measure UHI intensity with high-resolution local climate and satellite data. Identifying vulnerable populations and districts, integrating health and social impacts. Designing nature-based solutions (NBS) such as urban greening, permeable surfaces, and shading systems to reduce UHI impacts. Enhancing climate resilience by embedding UHI risk assessments into Antalya's forthcoming Heat Action Plan, ensuring policy uptake.\n\nThe project runs from Jan 2023 - Dec 2026, with a total cost of €146,000, funded by Horizon Europe (CLIMAAX FSTP) but seeking further resources for large-scale NBS implementation and monitoring systems.

project_info: Waste management (including waste recycling) - Inclusive Governance Models 4 a Greener Transition in the Mediterranean / GOV4GREENMED: The pilot study is about municipal solid waste management and focuses on using organic waste to produce organic fertilizers and raising awareness among farming communities about environmentally friendly agriculture. The pilot study aims to address the challenges of waste management and promote sustainable agriculture by using organic waste as a valuable resource. This capacity building will be provided by organizing trainings on issues such as separation of waste at source, importance of separate storage of organic waste, importance of separate storage of fertilizers, hazards of fertilizers, etc. for farmer groups and students in schools in agricultural regions, in addition to fertilizer production and application. The training will also focus on educating farmers about environmentally friendly agricultural practices and benefits of using organic fertilizers. By providing these training sessions, the pilot project aims to increase awareness and build the capacity of farmers and farming communities engaged in agriculture on a large scale, from young to old, women and men in Antalya. In order to support this effort, the pilot study will cooperate with both provincial and district municipalities to ensure a smooth and coordinated waste management process and a participatory governance model for waste management.

project_info: Nature-Based Solutions - EUropean_Trans-urban Reforestation for the Empowerment of Environmental Strategies (EU_TREES): This project proposal, developed within the scope of the INTERREG NEXT_MED call, aims to develop strategies to increase the resilience of green infrastructure in cities and urban areas to natural and anthropogenic risks through the implementation of nature-based solutions (NBS). In line with the specific objective 2.1 of the call text, which is to intervene in the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and the increase of energy efficiency through urban afforestation interventions, it aims to update the scientific knowledge and integrated practices available to local authorities to conduct experiments on environmental areas characterized by uncontrolled (unregulated) urbanization, degraded areas, waste areas. The project will identify the areas where pilot actions will be implemented, while also setting out general principles for the maintenance of the city and contributing to the solution of local problems in order to provide immediate tangible effects on the relevant problems.\n

Renewable energy - Mediterranean moNitoring of Environmental conteXt and maritime Traits in area designed to the Wind and solar farms Installation (MedNEXTWIN): The project aims to provide monitoring tools and procedures for transnational maritime spatial planning focused on the installation of wind or solar farms. The proposal, which is mainly aimed at public administrations, is based on two main objectives:
1) Implementation of methodological monitoring protocols for the collection of environmental information characterizing the potential of marine areas designated for the installation of wind or solar farms;
2) Development of procedures for assessing the suitability of these areas.
These objectives will be achieved through various activities, such as: implementation of innovative research tools for monitoring underwater noise; development and implementation of a transnational protocol for monitoring the distribution of sensitive target species; GIS-based implementation of the distribution of the main human activities in the maritime sector; capacity building of administrative authorities to deal with issues related to wind or solar farms; Public awareness of climate change and energy transition.

project_info: Transport - UrbanVind - Crowding Data Collection and Origin-Destination Data Estimation using BLE Scanning: Collecting data in public transport is a challenge in Europe. Cities struggle to collect important crowd data for operations and planning. Traditional solutions such as Automatic Passenger Counters are expensive and maintenance intensive, and techniques for determining Origin-Destination (OD) Matrices are often inaccurate. UrbanVind's CrowdFlow is an accurate, easy-to-install, and cost-effective software solution that provides real-time vehicle occupancy and passenger flow data. CrowdFlow uses Bluetooth to detect nearby devices and estimate passenger numbers. This prediction model, tailored to each city, provides real-time data to public transport authorities. By tracking Bluetooth devices, accurate OD Matrices are created. CrowdFlow, currently in beta, is showing an accuracy of around 75%. In order to improve service quality, Antalya in Turkey and Jurmala in Latvia need better OD data and real-time crowd predictions. They will implement CrowdFlow on their bus networks. The goal is to take Crowdflow to TRL 9. This project aims to deploy CrowdFlow at full operational scale for 6 months on two bus networks in Jurmala, Latvia and Antalya, Turkey to provide city operators with direct access to real-time crowd data and to estimate OD matrices. If successful, the system will have proven itself in different operational environments and urban contexts in different countries and cities of various sizes.

Waste management (including waste recycling) - Rehabilitation of Unregulated Landfills: Public Use Areas: Reassessment of the area to provide environmental and economic benefits such as recreation, agriculture, or renewable energy production.
Project in line with Antalya Metropolitan Municipality's Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan (SECAP) 4.4.2.1: Ecosystem Services, Biodiversity, and Green Spaces; 4.4.2.2: Water Management; 4.4.2.3: Urban, Infrastructure, and Waste Management; 4.4.2.4: Public Health and Disaster Management.
Antalya Metropolitan Municipality's Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan (SECAP) sets a target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 40% by 2030 and a vision of becoming a carbon-neutral city by 2050, providing an important roadmap for combating climate change. These targets are also in line with Turkey's national carbon neutrality goal for 2053. As one of the concrete steps Antalya has taken towards sustainable urbanization, this project will contribute to achieving both local and national climate goals by strengthening adaptation and mitigation actions against climate change.
The rehabilitation of unregulated landfill sites provides significant environmental, economic, and social benefits:

Environmental Benefits:
• Combating climate change by reducing greenhouse gas emissions caused by unregulated landfills
• Protection of surface and groundwater resources
• Supporting ecological sustainability by increasing soil fertility
• Using methane gas recovered for energy production
• Preferring local and drought-resistant plant species in afforestation efforts is important for climate change adaptation. 
• Rehabilitated areas will serve not only as green spaces but also as carbon sinks. 
Economic Benefits:
• Economic gains can be achieved through integration with biogas or renewable energy sources.
• Contributing to local economic development by creating tourism and recreation areas.
• Creating employment opportunities in waste management and environmental engineering.
Social Benefits:
• Improvement of public health
• Improvement of quality of life by increasing green spaces
• Increased awareness in the community about environmental issues and sustainability.
• Rehabilitated areas will be designed according to environmentally friendly design principles while being planned as open spaces for public use.

project_info:
Waste management (including waste recycling) - Sustainable Waste Management Using Electric Garbage Trucks: The integration of electric garbage trucks into municipal waste management systems supports sustainable urban development. The project aims to minimize carbon emissions by reducing fossil fuel use, help municipalities achieve their carbon neutrality goals, improve energy efficiency, and enhance air quality. The project will contribute to social well-being by improving the quality of urban life with low noise levels. 

In the designated pilot regions, technical and economic feasibility analyses of electric vehicle fleets will be conducted in the first phase, followed by the establishment of the necessary charging infrastructure. Training programs will be organized to ensure that municipal staff adapt to the new technology, and the efficiency of the process will be monitored through regular performance analyses. In this context, the integration of sustainable energy sources will also be evaluated.

Antalya Metropolitan Municipality's Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan (SECAP) sets a target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 40% by 2030 and a vision of becoming a carbon-neutral city by 2050, providing an important roadmap for combating climate change. These targets are also in line with Turkey's national carbon neutrality goal for 2053. Integrating electric garbage trucks into the waste management system will minimize carbon emissions by reducing fossil fuel use, thereby directly contributing to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions at the local level. At the same time, improving air quality and reducing noise pollution will enhance the quality of life for city residents, while long-term energy efficiency will lead to economic savings. This project is one of Antalya's concrete steps towards sustainable urbanization, strengthening climate change adaptation and mitigation actions, and contributing to the achievement of both local and national climate goals.
Environmental Benefits:
• Reduced fossil fuel consumption and lower carbon emissions.
• Reduced air pollution and improved urban air quality.
• Lower carbon footprint.
• Quieter urban environment due to reduced noise levels.
Economic Benefits:
• Long-term savings thanks to energy efficiency compared to diesel fuel costs.
• Financial support and grants for innovative and sustainable projects.
Social Benefits:
• Positive impact on public health.
• Acquisition of new skills for drivers and municipal staff and increased employment opportunities.
• Raising awareness among city residents about sustainability.

Waste management (including waste recycling) - Construction of Manavgat Wastewater Treatment Plant: The project aims to mitigate the negative impact on the environment and public health caused by pollutants contained in leachate from solid waste landfills through the use of advanced treatment techniques. Additionally, it seeks to protect surface and groundwater resources, assess the potential for wastewater reuse, and integrate innovative technologies into municipal waste management. 
This project involves the integration of advanced physical, biological, and chemical treatment methods to ensure the effective treatment of landfill leachate. First, the composition of the leachate will be characterized in detail, and appropriate treatment technologies will be identified. The implementation process consists of the following stages:
• Pre-treatment: Chemical treatment and sedimentation processes will be applied to remove solid particles and ensure suitable conditions prior to biological treatment. 
• Biological Treatment: Biological systems will be used to effectively treat leachate with high organic loads.
• Advanced Treatment: Membrane technologies (Ultrafiltration and Nanofiltration) will be used. 
• Recovery and Reuse: The reuse of treated water in industries and irrigation, etc., will be evaluated.
Approved by the Ministry of Environment, Urbanization, and Climate Change of the Republic of Turkey. The project will contribute to Antalya's 2030 sectoral greenhouse gas and energy reduction targets, including wastewater, agriculture, and livestock, with energy savings of 224,157 MWh and a greenhouse gas reduction target of 923,349 tCO2e for other sectors, as outlined in the Antalya Metropolitan Municipality's Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan.

	MWh Reduction 2030 Ton CO2e Reduction 2030
Building Emissions Reduction 10,372,980 4,576,934
Renewable Energy Emissions Reduction 744,000 377,208
Transportation Emissions Reduction 8,849,734 2,009,046
Waste, Wastewater, and Other Emissions Reduction 224,157 923,349
Total Reduction 20,190,870 7,886,537

Environmental Benefits: Untreated leachate contains high levels of toxic components. The use of advanced treatment systems will protect water resources and minimize negative impacts on the ecosystem. 
Economic Benefits: The reuse of treated leachate will contribute to the sustainable management of water resources while reducing water supply costs for municipalities. 
Social Benefits: The negative impact on the environment and public health caused by pollutants in landfill leachate will be eliminated. Furthermore, it will be an important step in raising environmental awareness and gaining public acceptance for sustainable waste management practices. It will contribute to personnel employment during the operation and construction phases.
Antalya Metropolitan Municipality's Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan (SECAP) sets a target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 40% by 2030 and a vision of becoming a carbon-neutral city by 2050, providing an important roadmap for combating climate change. These targets are also in line with Turkey's national carbon neutrality goal for 2053. This project, as one of the concrete steps Antalya has taken towards sustainable urbanization, will contribute to achieving both local and national climate goals by strengthening adaptation and mitigation actions against climate change.

Planning and feasibility studies have been completed. The project file has been approved by the Ministry of Environment, Urbanization, and Climate Change.

project_info: Health systems and services - Climate Urgency Response Through Awareness (CURA): The Mediterranean region is warming 20% faster than the global average, creating urgent risks such as severe heatwaves, floods, and water scarcity. CURA addresses not only the physical but also the psychological and social barriers (climate anxiety, eco-stress, cognitive dissonance) that limit effective climate action. The project strengthens cross-border cooperation between Antalya (TR), Mandras (GR), Tlemcen (DZ), and Valencia (ES) through awareness campaigns, digital tools, and governance frameworks. By combining scientific data with participatory engagement, CURA aims to improve preparedness, resilience, and long-term adaptive capacity in vulnerable Mediterranean cities.

The project integrates sustainable urban mobility and nature-based solutions into street design, aiming to reduce emissions, improve microclimate resilience, and increase social awareness. Pilot implementation will take place in Antalya's Pınarbaşı Neighborhood, with climate data monitoring, pedestrian traffic counts, and awareness activities. Health systems and services - Smart Green and Digital Twin Energy City Index: The overall objective of the project is to make European cities more resilient to climate change by developing data-driven decision-making processes using new-generation technologies such as digital twins, artificial intelligence, and blockchain. The project aims to enable cities to anticipate risks such as heat waves, energy poverty, and climate-related pressures on infrastructure, and to develop scenario-based solutions to these risks. It also contributes to updating cities' Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plans (SECAP) and supports the implementation of transparent, auditable, and accountable decision-making mechanisms at the local level, in line with European Union legislation.
Antalya Metropolitan Municipality, as a partner in this project, will contribute to the process of analyzing the city's current situation and identifying climate vulnerability risks. Within the scope of the project, it is planned to revise Antalya's current SECAP in line with its 2050 targets. Furthermore, analyses conducted using digital twin technology in areas such as heat waves, low-performance solar energy production, and energy poverty will support the development of the city's adaptation strategies. As a pilot city, Antalya will serve as an application area where artificial intelligence and data-driven decision support systems are tested in the field and produce outputs that guide investment planning.

project_info: Transport - Crowdflow - Crowding Data Collection And Origin-Destination Data Estimation Using Ble Scanning: Collecting data in public transportation is a challenging task in Europe. Cities struggle to collect important crowd data for operations and planning. Traditional solutions such as Automatic Passenger Counters are expensive and require intensive maintenance, and techniques for determining Origin-Destination (OD) Matrices are often inaccurate. UrbanVind's CrowdFlow is an accurate, easy-to-install, cost-effective software solution that provides real-time vehicle occupancy and passenger flow data. CrowdFlow uses Bluetooth to detect nearby devices and estimate passenger numbers. This prediction model, customized for each city, provides real-time data to public transport authorities. Accurate OD Matrices are created by tracking Bluetooth devices. Currently in beta, CrowdFlow shows approximately 75% accuracy. To improve service quality, Antalya in Turkey and Jurmala in Latvia need better OD data and real-time crowd forecasts. CrowdFlow will be implemented in bus networks. The goal is to bring CrowdFlow to TRL 9. This project aims to provide city operators with direct access to real-time crowd data and to deploy CrowdFlow at full operational scale for 6 months in two bus networks in Jurmala, Latvia, and Antalya, Turkey, to predict OD matrices. If successful, the system will have proven itself in different operational environments and urban contexts across various countries and cities of different sizes.

project_info: Land-Use - EU Partnership Project for Local Climate Action in Turkey: This project, coordinated by the Ministry of Environment, Urbanization, and Climate Change and financed by the European Union, aims to increase local decision-making and implementation capacity for climate action. project_info: Water management - AQUATIC URBAN ECOSYSTEMS ALIVE (AQUALIVE) - Flood-Resilient Parks for Climate-Resilient Cities: AQUALIVE addresses the growing climate pressures on Mediterranean cities such as floods, droughts, urban heat island effect, and biodiversity loss. The project introduces multifunctional flood-resilient parks as nature-based solutions (NbS) to reduce water-related hazards, regulate urban microclimates, and enhance biodiversity while creating recreational spaces. Six European and Mediterranean cities (including Antalya) will collaborate to design, test, and evaluate flood parks using an ecosystem services approach. Antalya Metropolitan Municipality will contribute with local data, stakeholder engagement, and trial testing methodologies in selected pilot areas. The project aims to shift urban water management paradigms, improve citizens' quality of life, and strengthen ecological resilience.

project_info: Land-Use - Investigation of the Effects of Forest Fire Risk on the Biodiversity of Forest Wildlife Under Threat of Extinction: Forest ecosystems in the Mediterranean face increasing fire risks due to climate change. The project, coordinated by Akdeniz University with partners including Antalya Metropolitan Municipality, NASA, and the General Directorate of Forestry, investigates how forest fire risks impact biodiversity, particularly wildlife species under extinction threat. Using advanced remote sensing and monitoring technologies (SAR, LIDAR via NASA GEDI, optical satellite data, terrestrial laser scanning), the project assesses fire-damaged ecosystems, biodiversity loss, and forest regeneration capacity.\nAntalya Metropolitan Municipality supports the project by providing local ecological data, stakeholder engagement, and contributing to spatial biodiversity analyses in burned areas. The outcomes will directly inform future forest management, biodiversity conservation, and climate adaptation strategies.

project_info: Sustainable food consumption/production - NON-CHEMICAL WEED MANAGEMENT IN MEDICINAL AND AROMATIC PLANTS (MAPs): The project aims to develop, disseminate, and implement environmentally friendly, non-chemical weed management methods for medicinal and aromatic plants (MAPs). The methods include mechanical, biological, and digital approaches to reduce reliance on chemical herbicides, aligned with the EU Green Deal objectives. Activities include training for early-career researchers, stakeholder workshops, and short-term scientific missions. The project enhances sustainable agricultural practices, reduces environmental and health risks, and fosters cross-European cooperation among 32 management committee members and partners from 19 COST countries.

project_info: Waste management (including waste recycling) - THE ROLE OF WASTE IN FOREST FIRES: COMMUNITY-BASED AWARENESS AND SOLUTION STRATEGIES: This project investigates the relationship between improperly disposed waste (plastic, glass, etc.) in forest areas and the increased risk of forest fires. Through citizen science and participatory methods, the project seeks to involve local communities in identifying fire risks linked to waste, reducing pollution, and strengthening cooperation among institutions. Key activities include awareness-raising campaigns, pilot studies in Antalya's forest zones, and active community engagement to reduce human-induced fire triggers. The project will improve ecological governance, enhance forest biodiversity protection, and empower citizens with practical fire prevention knowledge.

Other: Smart Urban Planning - DIGITAL TWINS FOR OPTIMIZED MANUFACTURING AND ECOLOGICAL URBAN DEVELOPMENT IN THE MEDITERRANEAN (DIOMEDE): DIOMEDE is a transnational initiative that uses digital twin technology, data-driven simulations, and advanced urban manufacturing to create sustainable and climate-resilient Mediterranean cities.
The project integrates real-time environmental monitoring, predictive analysis, and innovative materials to support urban decision-making and optimize resource efficiency.
DIOMEDE connects local authorities, research institutions, and innovation-focused organizations across Italy, Spain, Jordan, Egypt, and Turkey through a collaborative framework. By combining urban modeling, IoT sensor networks, AI-driven analysis, and contribution generation, the project will encourage cities to adopt sustainable development practices while enabling them to anticipate and mitigate climate-related risks.
The core methodology revolves around two key components in each participating city:
1. Digital Twin Application - Creating dynamic, data-driven 3D models that integrate real-time environmental, climatic, and infrastructural data to simulate urban scenarios and evaluate the impact of mitigation strategies. 
2. Localized Case Studies - Distribution of city-specific interventions focusing on priority challenges such as urban cooling strategies, circular economy applications, climate-adaptable infrastructure, and smart public spaces.

project_info: Nature-Based Solutions - EUROPEAN TRANS-URBAN REFORESTATION FOR THE EMPOWERMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL STRATEGIES (EU_TREES): Developed under the INTERREG NEXT_MED call, this project proposal aims to develop strategies to increase the resilience of green infrastructure in cities and urban areas against natural and human-induced risks through the implementation of nature-based solutions (NBS). In line with specific objective 2.1 of the call text, which focuses on interventions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and increase energy efficiency through urban afforestation interventions; it tends to update scientific knowledge and combined practices available to local authorities for conducting experiments on environmental areas characterized by uncontrolled (irregular) urbanization, degraded areas, and waste areas.\nThe project will identify areas where pilot actions will be implemented, while also establishing general principles for city maintenance and contributing to the resolution of local issues with the aim of providing immediate tangible effects on related problems.\n

Nature-Based Solutions - 

HOPE AND OPPORTUNİTY FOR RURAL PEOPLE AND ECOSYSTEMS - FOR BIODİVERSİTY (HOPE4BIO): “The HOPE4BIO project has been categorized under 'Nature-Based Solutions' as it integrates ecosystem-based approaches for climate adaptation, biodiversity conservation, and fire risk management in rural forest communities, while also including circular practices such as waste oil recycling and sustainable agriculture.”


Granting Authority and Grant Program: UNDP- Eco Future Grant Program
Project Summary: Rural communities on the outskirts of Antalya's forests are becoming increasingly vulnerable to the effects of climate change, particularly extreme heat, prolonged droughts, and rapidly spreading forest fires. Between 2019 and 2023, 60,000 hectares of land in Antalya were destroyed by forest fires. According to the General Directorate of Forestry, 95% of fires are caused by human activities, highlighting the urgent need for behavioral change and local ownership.
“Hope and Opportunities for Rural Communities and Ecosystems - In the Name of Biodiversity' project aims to increase the climate resilience of rural communities exposed to forest fire risk, with 9 forest villages in Akseki serving as pilot sites, by empowering them with knowledge, early response capacity, sustainable production practices, and biodiversity management. Specific objectives include:
•	To raise awareness and strengthen local capacities for the prevention of human-caused forest fires and early intervention in rural forest-urban interface communities.
•	Promoting sustainable and circular income generation models in forest villages, particularly through waste oil recycling, environmentally friendly soap production, and the cultivation of fire-resistant non-timber forest products such as carob, combining conservation and production.
•	Protecting biodiversity and natural resources by encouraging community participation in environmentally sensitive practices and low-impact land use.
•	Developing local governance and inter-institutional cooperation between municipalities, NGOs, and rural communities for integrated fire risk management and sustainable rural development.
Project Partners	: Turkish Foresters Association
Antalya Metropolitan Municipality

Sustainable food consumption/production - ANTALYA CLİMATE TABLES: The overall objective of the project is to contribute to the long-term transformation of climate-friendly food systems in Turkey by piloting a child- and community-focused model that promotes sustainable consumption, reduces food waste, empowers children, and supports intergenerational climate justice through education and inclusive local participation. The following activities will be implemented:
1- Hands-on Workshops ('Open Workshop: Climate-Friendly Production/Consumption Experiences'): 18 interactive workshops covering topics such as sustainable agriculture, zero waste, healthy eating, and climate-friendly food choices will be organized for children aged 10-14. Experiential learning methods such as gardening, composting, market visits, and food waste games will be used in these workshops. The expected outcome is that at least 300 children will increase their knowledge and practical skills, enabling them to make conscious, climate-friendly choices.
2- Development of the 'Antalya Climate-Friendly Production/Consumption Atlas': A child-friendly, interactive atlas will be created, featuring local producers, seasonal food calendars, zero-waste tips, and discovery routes throughout Antalya.
3- Climate-Friendly Chef Workshops: A series of chef workshops targeting girls aged 10-14 will be organized, providing training on sustainable cooking, recipe development, and preventing food waste. The program will include both theoretical and practical modules and will conclude with the creation of a 'Climate-Friendly Recipe Book' written by the participants. The expected outcome is the empowerment of 36 girls as 'climate-friendly chefs' and the dissemination of their recipes to a wider community.
4- Climate-Friendly Food Festival: A one-day festival will bring together children, families, local producers, and the public to celebrate and share the project's successes. Activities will include cooking workshops, zero-waste kitchen activities, games, and an exhibition of the atlas and recipe book. At least 500 community members—200 children and 300 adults—will participate in an impactful awareness-raising event promoting climate-friendly food systems.

Water management - HYDRA-NBS: NBS4WATER İN TURKEY AND GREECE: BUİLDİNG READİNESS TO ADOPT NATURE-BASED AND HYBRİD INFRASTRUCTURE TECHNOLOGİCAL APPROACHES FOR WATER RESİLİENCE: Granting Authority and Grant Program: PRIMA - Upscaling Nature-Based Solutions for Sustainable Water Management to Address Extreme Events in the Mediterranean
Project Summary: Water-related climate risks such as floods, droughts, water pollution, and seasonal variability are intensifying across the Mediterranean, threatening ecosystems, livelihoods, and urban infrastructure. Nature-Based Solutions (NBS) and hybrid infrastructure approaches offer integrated and cost-effective strategies to mitigate these risks while delivering multiple co-benefits such as biodiversity conservation, carbon sequestration, and community well-being. Despite their potential, cities and local authorities often encounter significant barriers to implementation. This project proposes a targeted capacity-building initiative designed to help six local and peri-urban administrations in Turkey and Greece reach Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 5 by supporting them in implementing and adapting a proven NbS prioritization and implementation framework. Key Objectives:
• To raise the TRL of participating municipalities and urban area administrations to level 5 using a proven NbS prioritization and decision-making framework.
• Jointly develop regionally adapted NbS strategies for Turkey and Greece that focus on reducing flood impacts, drought resilience, and water quality.
• Facilitate stakeholder collaboration across city and urban area boundaries, considering the cross-border needs of integrated water management.
• Strengthen the conditions for NbS integration, including access to finance and policy adoption.
• Enhance the capacity of city administrations and local partners for gender-sensitive NbS decision-making processes and create participatory spaces for policy planning.

Water management - REWATERMED: RE-DESİGNİNG WATER MANAGEMENT FOR CLİMATE ADAPTATİON İN THE MEDİTERRANEAN: Granting Authority and Grant Program: PRIMA CALLS-2025-SECTION 1
Project Summary: REWATERMED focuses on the widespread adoption of nature-based solutions (NBS) in line with the European Green Deal, the 2030 Biodiversity Strategy, and the 2030-2050 climate targets. The project promotes green, blue, and circular approaches to mitigate the effects of extreme weather events and water pollution caused by climate change, increase water security, and strengthen the resilience of ecosystems in the Mediterranean region. Testing the combined use of different types of nature-based solutions, conducting cost-effectiveness analyses, assessing socio-cultural impacts, and developing policy recommendations are among the project's key priorities. The project also aims to develop decision support tools for various Mediterranean ecosystems and explore hybrid solutions (integration of NBS with other infrastructure solutions).

project_info: Renewable energy - Solar Energy Production in Municipal Service Units: Currently, Kadıköy Municipality has no considerable investment in renewable energy in 2018. While renewable energy integration is harder to achieve in existing buildings, the performance of unlicensed photovoltaic (PV) power system applications is projected to reduce energy consumption and lower the number of electricity bills payable by the Municipality.Renewable energy practices adopted by public bodies are already supported by Development Agencies. Given the different types of financing coming into play over the course of time, Kadıköy Municipality has the capability to install a considerable number of unlicensed PV systems in very different structures such as warehouses, machine shops, and facilities, parking lots, etc. The current legislation allows for the performance of unlicensed applications up to 1 MW installed power and this value is reported to rise to 2.5 MW soon.It is projected that Kadıköy Municipality can install a PV system having a total of 1 MW power by 2030 through either roof systems or appropriate land applications. The electricity consumed by the Municipality totaled 8.2 million kWs in 2016. The said quantity corresponds to 0.02% of energy consumption throughout the city. Although the measures to be taken has no considerable impact on the reduction in urban energy consumption, they can serve both as a model to public members and a guide with experiences gained. project_info: Water management - Kadıköy Municipality Rainwater Collection Works: In line with the goals of protecting natural resources and implementing energy and water efficiency projects outlined in the Strategic Plan and the Climate Adaptation Action Plan, we have established \'Rainwater Collection Systems\' in five service units. Gutter and water tank cleaning, as well as pump maintenance and repairs, have been carried out. The rainwater collection system is used for garden irrigation and flushing at the Ecological Life Center and Aysel Abdullah Öğücü Girls' Dormitory, for car washes and street cleaning vehicles at the Kayışdağı Service Unit, and for flushing and educational purposes at the Design Workshop in Kadıköy. The fifth rainwater collection system, which we commissioned in 2024 at our Municipality's Temporary Animal Shelter, stores the stored rainwater and uses it for washing, garden irrigation, and cleaning purposes at the Shelter. As of the end of January 2025, the amount of rainwater collected in all service units where rainwater collection systems are installed reached 2,634 tons.

Waste management (including waste recycling) - Vale Verde Project: The Vale Verde Project, the first action of the Sustainability Trails Program, was developed with the aim of reducing the amount of recyclable waste sent to landfills, through the promotion of selective collection and environmental awareness. The initiative is coordinated with local cooperatives of recyclable material collectors, facilitating the proper disposal of waste and encouraging income generation.
An integral part of the actions of the Sustainability Trails Program, the Vale Verde Project aims not only to improve local environmental management, but also to raise awareness among the population about the relevance of sustainable waste management. As a result, educational campaigns will be organized in schools and local communities to provide information on the proper separation of waste and clarify the environmental impacts of incorrect disposal.
In the project proposal, there is also an incentive to participate in collection selective, promoting healthier eating by exchanging recyclable materials for food. Therefore, the Vale Verde Project, as one of the pillars of the Sustainability Trails Program, contributes to more efficient waste management and to the construction of a more sustainable future for the municipality of Francisco Morato.
According to the Municipal Plan for Integrated Solid Waste Management (PMGIRS/2023), the municipality established goals to implement municipal selective collection, invest in a Sorting and Recycling Center, and create a Municipal Reverse Logistics Plan. These actions, in line with the first steps of the Vale Verde Project, will instruct the population on the correct segregation of waste. In addition to bringing benefits to waste management, these actions will improve the income of the workers involved, contribute to public health, provide low-cost recyclable materials for industries, and reduce municipal expenses. The Project Vale Verde, therefore, aligns with the goals of PMGIRS/2023 and aims to promote efficient and sustainable waste management, contributing to the reduction of environmental vulnerability in Francisco Morato.

climate_hazard: Fire weather (risk of wildfires): Forest fires will affect infrastructures and the public health. These occurrences may lead to a reduction of the forest potential, pest increase, an increase in invasive species and loss of biodiversity and can affect even water quality and air quality.The recurrence of fires, ie, the number of years between each fire in a specific site, is likely to increase, exacerbating the 'fire> invasive> fire cycle' and the inherent forest management problems. Frequent fires alone may lead to a predominance of shrub vegetation. In this situation, the elimination of the native species seed bank will make it easier to invasive species of subtropical origin to proliferate, such as some acacias already existing in the mountains as naturalized that benefict from the new climatic conditions. | Coastal flooding (incl. sea level rise): Variations in the marine flood regime will be essentially related to the sea level rise. Considering the scenarios of elevation between +0,6 m and +1,0 m and gall dimensions from 9.6 m to 10.0 m, an increase of the potentially flooded area is expected affecting the community, transports network, infrastructures, among others. These sea level rise and the consequantly sand reduction is also a point of concern since this reduction is estimated to be between 20% and 40% by 2100 and is more important on the narrowest beaches of the region. | Urban flooding: The catchments of the streams that cross the municipality of Sintra have an area of a few tens of km2 and a time of concentration of the order of an hour. The realisation of the scenarios of increased risk of intense precipitation and flooding will cause an increase in the values of rainfall runoff generated in the basins may exceed the flow capacity of the natural hydrographic network or urban drainage systems. | Other: Insect Infestation: It is expected the increase of diseases as well as the risk of invasion by new species of tropical or subtropical climate regions. It is also very possible that the growth rates of pests and diseases already present are stimulated by temperature increase, especially when is possible to have several generations per year. The temperature increase in the winter, accompanied by high humidity, may favor the expansion of some pathogens. Water stress can make trees more susceptible to diseases in the most arid areas, where they can increase the damage caused by, for example, insect borers. | Infectious disease: It is expected the increase of diseases as well as the risk of invasion by new species of tropical or subtropical climate regions. It is also very possible that the growth rates of pests and diseases already present are stimulated by temperature increase, especially when there is a possibility to have several generations per year. The temperature increase in the winter, accompanied by high humidity, may favour the expansion of some pathogens. Water stress can make trees more susceptible to diseases in the most arid areas, where they can increase the damage caused by, for example, insect borers. | Extreme heat: High temperatures and extreme hot days / heat waves may lead to the reduction of crops quality resulting in a lost of productivity. It may also lead to infrastructure degradation due to excessive heat (deformation of the asphalt due to melting) and lead to a decrease in buildings thermal comfort and in the urban areas bioclimatic comfort. It will also affect the public health. These occurrences may lead to a reduction of the forest potential, pest increase, an increase in invasive species and loss of biodiversity and also affect water quality. In the case of the Municipality of Sintra, due to its proximity to the ocean and the Sintra Mountains, heat waves are expected to be less intense.
project_info: Energy efficiency (including public lighting) - street lighting with LED luminaries: The municipality of Sintra has carried out the requalification of street lighting grid through the installation of LED luminaries, which constitutes a project of relevant impact in terms of the improvement of sustainability.In 2020 910 LED luminaires were installed and in 2021 4063 LED luminaires were installed.The requalification of the street lighting in the municipality of Sintra represents a very important investment, since it constitutes a project with hight impact on the improvement of sustainability in the municipality and because it constitutes an incentive to pedestrian and cycling mobility, increases the security of citizens and enhances the public space. The requalification of the street lighting grid has given the municipality a new vitality, both as a space conducive to the performance of outdoor shows and as a meeting and socialisation space that contributes to the social and economic development of the city.

project_info: Public and green spaces - Urban park of Rinchoa - Fitares: The urban park of Rinchoa - Fitares, in the parish of Rio de Mouro, was characterized by mediterranean vegetation and eucalyptus trees and it was rehabilitated and transformed into a park with an approximate area of 12 hectares. With the rehabilitation of this park the municipality intended to enable citizens to enjoy green spaces of quality with leisure equipment and moments of relaxation, in a natural landscape with diversity of fauna and flora associated with riverside areas. The park was inaugurated in 2015 and the project represented an investment of around € 160,000. In a second phase pedestrian bridges were built with the aim of improving the pedestrian paths that cross the existing water line, replacing the previous walkways of precarious nature with modern and secure integrated solutions in the landscape. Other: Carbon-neutral balance - Maia Living Lab: Net Zero Carbon City: O BaZe - Maia Living Lab: Net Zero Carbon City combined actions of sustainable mobility, energy efficiency, renewable energy, circular economy and citizen involvement, in order to build a scalable and replicable urban ecosystem to promote decarbonization. This entire ecosystem was continuously monitored, ensuring that the consumption and production of resources were managed in an intelligent and sustainable way, supporting the optimization of processes aimed at reducing the economic, social and environmental impacts inherent to the global demand for energy. Supported by a Smart Meters architecture, considering the potential of the Internet-of-Things (IoT) phenomenon and Cloud computing systems to empower managers with advanced tools for monitoring, controlling and optimizing infrastructures and equipment. The implemented solutions offered an interactive experience for experience, in urban space, moments of understanding and learning regarding the management of city resources. On the other hand, and in a more dematerialized concept, numerous training actions were carried out, combined with the promotion of co-creation spaces by and for citizens, translating high-level knowledge, actions and language into concrete actions that are easy to understand, but have high added value. The development of the project and the symbiosis of the technologies described above, which are interdisciplinary, were supported by a set of factors that guaranteed the successful implementation of the proposed measures and actions. In addition to the participants in the consortium, with extensive experience in implementation and research projects in the field of this candidacy, the integration of various stakeholders also stands out, in a logic of interaction between the municipality, knowledge centers, companies, industries and citizens. The definition of actions was based on the work previously carried out by different partners so that multiple innovative actions could be tested in a delimited space, which as a whole had never been tested simultaneously on national territory. Given the short implementation period, the selected solutions are already on the market (TRL8 or 9) but have never been tested in such an integrated way and so close to the citizen.

ii)	PT: Circular Economy and Environment - Action: Pay-As-You-Throw (PAYT) System; Green Roofs; Community Composting; Efficient Water Management; Permaculture; Air Quality

Other: Community involvement and energy efficiency - EYES HEARTS HANDS - URBAN REVOLUTION (EHHUR): EHHUR aims to test and validate concrete and disruptive solutions to concrete socioeconomic and cultural challenges, paying particular attention to the themes of social exclusion, energy poverty and the transition to more sustainable energy sources.

Through a diverse set of activities, the project aims to achieve the following objectives:
•	Develop a holistic methodology based on the three dimensions of urban transformation: Eyes, Hearts and Hands
•	Involve public and private representatives and the rest of the community in the decision-making process and co-design of the local urban environment, thus creating an open and permanent communication path
•	Validate the proposed methodology and the technological, social and financial solutions/tools created, in the 7 chosen European demonstrators, in full respect for the local heritage and characteristics specific to each person
•	Establish a financing support system/framework that combines a traditional approach with innovative business models, in order to guarantee the accessibility of investment
•	Support the implementation and generalization of the principles of the New European Bauhaus and European Union Missions through capacity development and training at local level, with a view to replicating the proposed methodology at local, regional and national level. 

EHHUR's approach is based on the involvement of the population and the application of co-design principles as the “backbone” of its methodological approach, through the implementation of a set of social innovation activities designed not only to involve, but also to ensure the participation of key entities and groups of citizens.

The project is thus structured under three key principles and respective components, namely:

EYES 
Aesthetically appealing urban transformation and socially accepted:
•	Cultural heritage and infrastructure / traditional architecture, design and culture
•	Local resources, in terms of materials, techniques, but also human capital and local skills
•	Awareness, involvement and commitment of multiple stakeholders

HEARTS
A socially fair urban transformation:
•	'energy solidarity' approaches to situations of energy poverty, such as through the creation of Communities of Renewable Energy (CER)
•	Vulnerable stakeholders/citizens, including people of advanced age and/or in situations of social exclusion
•	Promotion of gender equality with a view to reducing inequalities

HANDS
An urban transformation that aims at concrete commitment actions to achieve sustainability:
•	“Energy solidarity” approaches to situations of energy poverty, such as through the creation of Energy Communities Renewable (CER) 
•	Vulnerable stakeholders/citizens, including people of advanced age and/or in situations of social exclusion
•	Promotion of gender equality with a view to reducing inequalities

Other: Energy Poverty - URBACT - Innovation Transfer Networks (ITN - Innovation Transfer Networks): It is a European territorial cooperation program that promotes sustainable and integrated urban development. Funded by the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF), it aims to promote sustainable urban development through cooperation between cities, so that together they can find solutions to common urban challenges.
Through the establishment of transnational exchange and learning networks, participation in the URBACT program provides the opportunity to work with other European cities with a view to a specific public policy challenge.
The Municipality will be able to test new ideas and solutions through the use of URBACT methodological tools, namely the well-known integrated and participatory approach as URBACT Method. The Innovation Transfer Networks (ITN) in the URBACT program are one of the main tools to promote the sharing of good practices between European cities. 
These networks aim to transfer projects that were financed under the Urban Innovative Actions (UIA) to other cities in the European Union. Thus, the UIA, currently called EUI (European Urban Initiative), has the mission of financing innovative pilot projects that address complex urban challenges and that serve as 'living laboratories' to test transformative ideas. The participation of the Municipality of Maia in the EmPowerIngUs Network represents a strategic opportunity to address essential urban challenges and allow the Municipality to align with European Union goals in terms of sustainability, inclusion and innovation. On the other hand, this Network is based on an example of good urban practices that has the potential to transform citizens' quality of life, especially in areas affected by hidden energy poverty.

Work in progress:\n- Construction of a rainwater collector on Rua Dr. Artur Figueiroa Rego and Rua das Estufas, in concrete manilas, with a nominal diameter between 600 and 1000 mm, starting at the roundabout at the intersection of Rua Professor Abílio Moniz Barreto and Rua Dr. Artur Figueiroa Rego, up to its discharge point in the watercourse called “Vala da Palhagueira” (Vala dos Texugos), according to the drawings.\n- Construction of a Retention/Infiltration Basin;- Construction of a retention/infiltration basin at the discharge point, which corresponds to the watercourse known as Vala da Palhagueira (Texugos Valley), to dampen the inflow flow coming from this rainwater collector, and minimize the risk of flooding/flooding in the Vala da Palhagueira (Vala dos Texugos);

project_info: Other: Climate Change - Creation of an alert, prevention and monitoring system for areas vulnerable to climate risks in the municipality\n: The creation of an environmental monitoring system for areas currently subject to climate risk in the municipality is essential to increase the resilience of the municipality of Caldas da Rainha in the face of climate change. This project consists of implementing sensors that will evaluate various environmental variables, taking advantage of the exemplary capacity already installed in the municipality with the LoRaWAN network, creating a solid database for the due and necessary environmental monitoring, related to the greatest environmental risks identified. This fact will also enable the municipality to conduct its adaptation decisions in the near future in a more sustainable manner. This project will be submitted at the 2nd call of CLIMAAX.

project_info: Water management - Hydraulic optimization of the Caldas da Rainha system\n: The main objective of the project to be carried out is the Hydraulic and Energy Optimization of the Caldas da Rainha Distributor System (with almost half the length of the municipal network) and, consequently, to obtain a significant improvement in hydraulic functioning, a better service to the population, and the reduction of both energy costs and water losses in the supply network, with, at the municipality level, unbilled water (ANF) is 27.4% of the input into the system, a value that is intended to be reduced with a view to mitigating this economic and environmental scourge.\nThus, the overall objective of the Project will be to analyze the current situation in the Caldas da Rainha Sub-System and detail a technically-economically advantageous hydraulic solution, which creates conditions to reduce energy costs and place water losses at a much lower level and which, consequently, can free up economic and environmental resources, simultaneously improving the quality of care for the population
